Cigarette Smoking Cigarette smoking has been shown
to be causally related to lower bone density, increased bone
mineral loss, and increased risk of fracture in males and
females.7, 12, 18, 28, 34 Th ere are several mechanisms that place
smokers at increased risk of poor bone health. Nicotine and 
cadmium in tobacco smoke are toxic to osteoblasts. Tobacco
smoke appears to reduce intestinal calcium absorption, and 
smokers generally have lower intakes of vitamin D and lower 
serum levels of 25-hydroxyvitamin D compared with nonsmok-
ers.34 Smokers are more likely to consume excessive amounts
of alcohol than are nonsmokers, which can adversely impact
bone health
